title: The Best Group Chat
premise: Odile Lockridge, seventeen and effectively the parent of her two younger siblings, joins a senior class group chat created to answer a viral college essay prompt: 'Who are you when no one is watching?' The anonymous confessions spiral into a school-wide obsession, and when Odile's own post — about raising her siblings while her mother works nights — leaks, she becomes both a symbol and a target. As the chat's moderators gain real power over reputations, Odile must expose how the honest-question game has been weaponized, reclaim her own story in her final college audition, and choose a future defined by who she is, not what she's survived.
about_author: Ines Quintana is a former high school debate coach from the Rio Grande Valley who writes about teenagers carrying adult-sized lives. She believes the truest stories are the ones we tell strangers online before we can say them out loud.

chapters.title: The Question on Page One
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Between packing lunches and covering her sister's shift anxiety, Odile skims the college essay prompt and scoffs at it — until her best friend Priya adds her to a new senior class group chat built around it. Beat: weary skepticism cracking into curiosity.

chapters.title: Rules of the Room
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The chat's three anonymous moderators post rules: real answers only, no screenshots, no names. Early posts are shallow, but one confession about a father's gambling lands hard. Beat: the thrill of a room where nobody knows your face.

chapters.title: Third Parent
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A chaotic morning — little brother Marcus misses the bus, mom's night shift runs long — shows readers Odile's double life. At school she watches classmates perform normalcy. Beat: exhaustion sharpening into quiet resentment.

chapters.title: First Honest Thing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with intercut chat messages. Late at night, half-asleep, Odile posts anonymously about eating cereal for dinner so the kids won't know there's nothing else. By morning it has forty replies. Beat: terrifying relief at being seen.

chapters.title: Priya Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya recognizes Odile's voice in the post and says nothing, wrestling with loyalty versus the no-names rule. Meanwhile moderator 'Vesper' begins curating the best confessions into daily threads. Beat: intimacy and its small betrayals.

chapters.title: The Audition List
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The performing arts program posts final audition requirements: a personal monologue drawn from 'a moment that made you.' Odile panics — her whole life is the moment she can't afford to admit. Beat: dread as the essay question follows her offline.

chapters.title: Vesper Ascendant
chapters.summary: New student Theo's POV. Theo, one of the anonymous moderators, discovers his curation threads are shaping social hierarchies — kids court him for inclusion. He tells himself it's harmless. Beat: the first taste of power and the excuse-making that follows.

chapters.title: Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A popular athlete confesses to an eating disorder; a quiet girl admits she's the family translator for her undocumented parents. The school's cliques visibly loosen. Odile feels hope — maybe honesty can be a place to live. Beat: fragile optimism.

chapters.title: Mom's Night Off
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mom takes the kids to a late movie; Odile gets two hours alone and realizes she doesn't know what she likes anymore. She drafts an audition monologue and deletes it twice. Beat: grief for the self she postponed.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Against the rules, Vesper screenshots Odile's cereal post and sends it to a friend 'off the record.' It spreads within hours. Beat: casual carelessness becoming catastrophe.

chapters.title: Named
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The school pieces together that the post is hers. Pity, gossip, and a teacher's well-meaning intervention make her feel like a case file instead of a person. Marcus overhears kids mocking their dinners. Beat: shame turning to fury.

chapters.title: Sainthood Is Just Another Cage
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Classmates now treat Odile as either a saint or a sob story; even her essay draft feels like performance. Priya urges her to fight back, but Odile just wants it to stop. Beat: the cost of being everyone's symbol.

chapters.title: Moderator Wars
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Vesper begins posting 'follow-up investigations' into other confessions, exposing a cheater and a closeted student without consent. Theo objects; Vesper threatens to reveal the moderator identities. Beat: power openly corrupting.

chapters.title: Marcus's Answer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV (younger sibling). Twelve-year-old Marcus secretly joins the chat under a fake account and posts about being raised by a sister who forgot to be a teenager. Odile reads it at 1 a.m. and breaks down. Beat: love and guilt colliding.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile figures out Theo is a moderator and corners him. He confesses the leak's origin and gives her the evidence trail against Vesper — but helping means breaking anonymity rules herself. Beat: alliance forged in shared complicity.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, Odile, and Theo plan to take the archive to the principal, knowing exposure will burn every anonymous confessor, including friends. They debate whether protection or truth matters more. Beat: moral weight settling on young shoulders.

chapters.title: Vesper Unmasked
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Before they can act, Vesper preemptively doxxes Theo and announces the chat's endgame: a public assembly reading of 'the year's most honest posts.' Odile's is first on the list. Beat: trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Ruin
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the assembly days away, Odile stops fighting the reading and instead rewrites her audition monologue around the truth on her own terms — claiming authorship before it can be stolen. Beat: defiance replacing fear.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the assembly, Vesper performs Odile's post as spectacle; Odile walks onstage mid-reading and finishes it herself, then names what Vesper did. The room turns. Beat: climax — reclaiming the narrative publicly.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Vesper faces consequences; the chat dissolves, but smaller honest friendships survive it. Theo accepts his part and apologizes to Odile without asking forgiveness. Beat: accountability without easy redemption.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile performs her monologue — not the tragedy, but the morning she chose to stay — and gets into the program with a scholarship that includes housing, making leaving possible without abandoning anyone. Beat: triumph earned, not gifted.

chapters.title: Who We Are When the Labels Are Off
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, closing. Moving day: Mom takes a day shift at last, Marcus steps up, Priya promises weekly calls. Odile starts a new group chat with the people who earned their names. Beat: found family intact, identity chosen, door open.
